result.title: SelfImprove-Bench: Evaluating Generalization in Self-Improving Agents
result.summary: Recursively self-improving (RSI) systems are increasingly viewed as a promising means of accelerating progress toward artificial general intelligence. They aim to autonomously improve their capabilities by refining their working pipelines and recursively improving the strategies that guide subsequent refinements, with gains generalizing to unseen scenarios.However, existing evaluations lack reliable metrics to distinguish capability gains from scenario fitting, sustainable and extensible protocols for unseen tasks and difficulties, and fine-grained attribution of improvement to evolution traces. To this end, we propose SelfImprove-Bench,an RSI evaluation framework that organizes tasks into three primary capabilities (i.e., Exploring, Planning, Reasoning) as scenarios for guiding model evolution. We instantiated the tasks on games for controllability and reproducibility, and pairs them with scalable generation and orchestration driven by task templates and difficulty coefficients. Beyond task-level scores, SelfImprove-Bench organizes evaluation into generalization ladder levels G0 to G4 that measure how far gains transfer from training conditions. Experiments reveal that the evolutionary gains of existing RSI methods are inconsistent across generalization levels.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SelfImprove-Bench，以游戏任务和可扩展难度设计评测自我改进智能体，并用 G0–G4 泛化阶梯区分能力提升与场景拟合。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「泛化阶梯」与对演化轨迹的改进归因，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练收益分配、跨任务泛化和能力提升评价提供参照，需核查其指标能否迁移。
